mission_dimensions.track_definition: mission.md section 5: Track A = variant-independent WWOX loss of function; Track B = variant or allele-class specific (e.g. the Q230P missense class); Track C = repurposing, which is a method of reaching A or B, not a third lesion class
mission_dimensions.route_definition: RECUPERO_PROFONDO = deep recovery of the lost function; BENEFICIO_PRECOCE = concrete partial benefit, symptomatic control or protection of function, with paediatric feasibility and time in view
mission_dimensions.route_note: Symptomatic network lever on an unmeasured premise; the single decisive experiment is specified, not run.
mission_dimensions.the_two_dimensions_are_independent: a card keeps both: a variant-independent lever can be a partial-benefit lever, and a lesion-specific one can aim at deep recovery

candidate.name: Bumetanide and the chloride gradient (E_GABA premise)

disease_assertions.source: GSE156243 (PMID 34268881 deposit); descriptive panel by scientist-c, disease-models/wwox/research/drug_repurposing/w2_therapeutic_it2_20261027/README.md

context.disease_id: WWOX-deficient human cerebral organoid model (engineered knockout; NOT a patient allele; no amyloid)
context.genotype: WWOX knockout versus wild type (4 versus 2 libraries, one laboratory)

disease_assertions.measured_result_note: Ratio 0.24, 0.29, 0.13, 0.14 in the four knockouts and 0.29, 0.30 in the two wild types: not higher in knockouts, so no transcript-level hint of a more depolarising chloride gradient; SLC12A2 is flat and SLC12A5 is higher in two knockouts. Composition-confounded (GAD1 about ten-fold different), transcript not function, direction left UNKNOWN.

disease_assertions.source: GSE156243 descriptive panel by scientist-c (the marker pattern behind DL-MECH-035)

context.disease_id: WWOX-deficient human cerebral organoid model (engineered knockout; NOT a patient allele; no amyloid)

disease_assertions.measured_result_note: GABRB2 about a quarter and GABRB3 about half of wild type; the same libraries carry more GABAergic-lineage transcripts. Reduced receptor transcript is not a chloride gradient.

p4_fields.endpoint_pursued: Perforated-patch GABA reversal potential in Wwox-deficient versus isogenic neurons or slices at matched maturity, with NKCC1 and KCC2 protein and the GABA response itself; only if depolarising, a bumetanide effect on bursting.
p4_fields.functional_evidence_available: None: no chloride, E_GABA, NKCC1 or KCC2 protein, or GABA pharmacology has been measured in any Wwox system.
p4_fields.temporal_or_model_limit: Depolarising GABA is an early developmental state; the window may be closed in the juvenile slice.

cellular_context.target_expression: SLC12A2 and SLC12A5 transcripts are present in the week-15 organoid.

p4_card.identity: Bumetanide (approved loop diuretic). Identity check 2026-10-27: ChEMBL_37 curates its mechanism as inhibition of the NKCC2 transporter only; NKCC1 appears in three activity rows (two single-concentration inhibition readings in HEK cells and one fitted value in HT-29 cells by rubidium uptake), so the NKCC1 target of the repurposing idea is an activity-table fact, not a curated mechanism.
p4_card.indication_and_transfer: Only IF GABA is depolarising in Wwox-deficient neurons at the relevant age; unmeasured. The CNS penetration of bumetanide is a known limitation (map R-07).
p4_card.novelty_for_woree: Map R-07 stands as INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE. New: (1) the transcript-level ratio in the one human knockout deposit does not point to a depolarising gradient (descriptive, confounded); (2) the target-identity note above; (3) the single experiment is written out with controls. Neonatal-seizure and autism trials exist (titles retrieved: NEMO open-label dose-finding in newborn hypoxic-ischaemic seizures, PMID 25765333; a phase 3 autism programme, PMID 35292925; a phase 2 autism trial, PMID 32730977); their outcomes were NOT read here.
p4_card.mechanism: Target NKCC1 (SLC12A2); wanted direction: lower intracellular chloride so GABA hyperpolarises; sign depends on an unmeasured quantity.

external_not_wwox_evidence: ChEMBL_37 mechanism and activity rows for CHEMBL1072

for: GABAergic-lineage and receptor-subunit transcripts differ in the knockout organoid.
against: No transcript-level hint of a raised NKCC1:KCC2 ratio in the knockout organoid.
Poor CNS penetration is a known limitation.

p4_card.pharmacology: NKCC1 activity: one fitted value and two single-concentration readings in ChEMBL (values in the README). IT8 P3 2026-10-29: GtoPdb (human, one document) gives pIC50 5.60 for NKCC1 and 6.48 for the kidney transporter, so the drug is about 7.6 fold more potent on the renal target; mouse brain to plasma ratio about 0.015 to 0.02 and efflux at the blood-brain barrier (abstract level); at the single intravenous dose reported, far above the diuretic range, modelled free brain concentrations were in the NKCC1-inhibitory range, and diuretic-range doses do not reach neuronal inhibitory concentrations; a close derivative that does not inhibit NKCC1 reproduces some CNS effects (PMID 30248303), so a CNS effect of the drug is not evidence of NKCC1 action. A systemic bumetanide response therefore requires verification of relevant exposure, that is a free brain concentration in the NKCC1 range of about 1.5 to 2.5 micromolar; arithmetic from the mouse figures (brain unbound fraction 6 to 17 percent for three diuretics, brain to plasma ratio about 0.015 to 0.02) puts the corresponding total brain concentration at about 9 to 42 micromolar, an assumption-bound figure and not a prediction (the neonatal maturation of the barrier and efflux in the Wwox-null model is not addressed by these sources; the human plasma concentration is not stated in the US label excerpt read, so it is UNKNOWN here). The premise test is ex vivo with the drug in the bath, where the NKCC1 range of about 1.5 to 2.5 micromolar is the exposure target.

GRIN and rat rows are at the reading depth stated per row.
scope_of_checks.card_inferences_owed_audit: Every statement marked INFERENZA, and every card-level synthesis, is owed a blind audit by someone other than the producer.

p4_card.predictions: Registered: if GABA is hyperpolarising in the knockout at the age studied, the card closes; if depolarising, bumetanide at a brain-relevant exposure lowers burst frequency, and a negative result at that exposure does not refute the premise.
p4_card.next_measurement: Gramicidin perforated-patch E_GABA in Wwox-deficient versus parental neurons or slices at three ages (including the earliest culturable), NKCC1 and KCC2 protein by immunoblot or immunostaining, GABA puff response; controls: wild type and heterozygote, bicuculline or gabazine sensitivity, an NKCC1 knockdown arm in place of the drug; the compound is applied in the bath ex vivo, and a systemic response requires verification of relevant exposure (IT8 P3, restated IT9 P4a); discriminating result: a depolarised E_GABA specific to the knockout that an NKCC1 manipulation shifts.
p4_card.value_added: Names the premise measurement, corrects the target identity record, adds a transcript-level negative hint.
p4_card.clinical_census: Clinical census, ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, 2026-10-20 (drug_repurposing/clinical_census_20261020.md): seven queries returned no registered WOREE interventional study; it answers seven queries against one registry on one date and a missing hit does not prove that no study exists. Not re-run for this card.

card_conventions: IPOTESI throughout; the bridge forces it. No score, rank, probability or blended index is carried.
directional_summary compares signs only where target, endpoint and every context dimension match; UNRESOLVED is a statement about the record, not about the biology.
Every disease-side row from the Drosophila article is NOT WWOX-DEE EVIDENCE; the organoid rows are exploratory transcript analyses of one deposit.
Abstract-level statements from PubMed are labelled abstract_only; none carries a receipt.
label_lookup is NOT_ATTEMPTED in the bridge: the bridge has no network. The openFDA adapter was run separately and is recorded in lucas_clarke_followup_20261026/compounds_and_sources.md.
No dose, route, schedule or paediatric suitability appears; assay concentrations of the sources are deliberately not reproduced.
